messages:
michael: Quick idea — proposal to slim the request path by moving non-hot-path concerns (validation, header enrichment, heavy transforms) into a plugin layer sitting in front of the runtime.
priyanka: what do you mean by 'plugin layer'? sidecar or an in-process hook?
michael: sidecar-style plugin container managed by the gateway, but with a thin compatibility shim in the runtime so legacy callers keep working. The shim would be an opt-in flag initially.
leo: main tradeoff is extra network hop and cold-start for new plugin code. latency impact test needed. :thinking_face:
anya: Also need to think about auth/tenant propagation. If we move validation out, we must guarantee identical semantics and audit logs.
zheng: +1 on audit. We should keep a canonical validation spec (json-schema + behavioral tests) so plugins are verifiable.
priyanka: Another concern: how do we do graceful rollout? If plugin has a bug we must be able to fallback to core runtime validation quickly.
michael: plan: 1) implement plugin API (sync/async hooks), 2) default a no-op plugin, 3) provide a reference validation plugin, 4) rollout behind feature flag per-tenant with canary traffic. Fallback: runtime will have a strict-pass-through fallback mode.
leo: can we quantify perf? suggestion: add a benchmark microbenchmark testing per-request overhead for: (a) in-process validation, (b) local sidecar loopback, (c) networked plugin (tcp).
anya: Will also need tracing propagation + span naming so we can see costs per plugin. Add contract-level metrics (validation_lat_ms, plugin_error_rate).
priyanka: On contracts: propose we bind plugin version in the model-profile registry so we know which runtime+plugin combos are supported. That avoids weird combos in production.
zheng: One more: how do we handle tenant-specific custom rules? We can't deploy unique plugin binaries for every tenant. Maybe compose rule sets (host a ruleset store and plugin reads tenant rules at runtime).
michael: Exactly — plugin binary stays generic, rules are tenant-configured. The ruleset service would be read-through cached in plugin. We'll add a ruleset version header to requests for reproducibility.
priyanka: Security: plugin runs in infra-managed sandbox, RBACed access to KMS only for allowed tenants. We need threat model doc for plugin layer.
leo: For rollout timeline: spike (2w) to prove perf & tracing, RFC doc (1w) with API surface, prototype plugin (3w), canary (2w). Total ~8 weeks. Thoughts?
anya: Sounds reasonable. Add time for test-suite: property tests + regression evals (we should run sample prompts that previously caught issues).
zheng: I'll own the benchmark and tracing instrumentation spike. michael: I'll own the prototype and RFC. priyanka: I'll draft the rollout/runbook + fallback playbook.
infra-bot: deploy-checklist: ensure canary routing, feature-flag toggle, and alerting (validation_plugin_error_rate > 1% for 5m).
leo: small nit — we should version the plugin API semantically and plan a migration strategy for v1 -> v2. No breaking changes without a deprecation period.
michael: agreed. I'll include semver policy in the RFC.
anya: ok let's sync tomorrow 10am to review the RFC spike results.
priyanka: added to calendar. :calendar:
michael: thanks all — recording key actions: (michael) prototype & RFC, (zheng) perf + tracing spike, (priyanka) rollout doc & runbook, (anya) tests/regression harness.
leo: one more: include a small compatibility test harness that runs runtime-only vs plugin-on paths and diffs outputs to detect semantic drift.
zheng: noted. will include in benchmark plan.
michael: closing loop — if spikes look good we'll open follow-up PRs and schedule a canary in 6 weeks.
priyanka: cool.
